question: Can two independently specified unpaired appearance objectives support a hard-selected bounded explicit look when they agree, while forcing a hard identity fallback when the observed reference appearance is already matched or the inferred operators disagree?

policy.selection: hard argmin of the validation mean normalized residual ratio across both frozen objectives; never average operators or RGB

allowed_actions: reuse the frozen O0 cube-preserving explicit flow and existing SWD/RFF-MMD objectives without changing their implementations
hard-select one whole explicit operator after validation
fall back to exact identity on weak appearance change, canonicalizer disagreement, insufficient validation improvement or structural failure
use the local RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU under deterministic settings
forbidden_actions: claim either canonicalizer identifies the hidden digital-to-film operator
average candidate operators, velocity grids or RGB outputs
use project film pixels, current stock pools, confirmation populations or owner preference votes
relax thresholds or change scenario generation after observing formal output
train a neural RGB generator or route by content/source/scanner identity
promote a stock, mode, product renderer or calibrated claim
claim_ceiling: synthetic mechanism evidence for a hard-selected bounded film-inspired appearance matcher with canonicalizer sensitivity and identity fallback; no real-film operator, stock, mode, calibration, preference or product claim
